sentences.chinese: 勒怒，遣宇文乞得龜擊廆，廆遣皝距之。
sentences.literal: Le was angry, dispatched Yuwen Qidegui to strike Kuang; Kuang dispatched Huang to resist him.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Le flew into a rage and sent Yuwen Qidegui against Murong Hui; Hui sent Murong Huang to hold the line.

sentences.chinese: 以裴嶷為右部都督，率索頭為右翼，命其少子仁自平郭趣柏林為左翼，攻乞得龜，克之，悉虜其眾。
sentences.literal: He appointed Pei Yi commander of the right division, led the Suotou as the right wing, ordered his younger son Ren from Pingguo toward Bailin as the left wing, attacked Qidegui, overcame him, and took all his host captive.
sentences.idiomatic: He named Pei Yi commander of the right wing, led the Suotou tribesmen on the right, and sent his youngest son Murong Ren from Pingguo toward Bailin on the left; they crushed Qidegui and carried off his entire army.

sentences.chinese: 乘勝拔其國城，收其資用億計，徙其人數萬戶以歸。
sentences.literal: Riding victory he took their capital city, gathered supplies reckoned in the hundreds of millions, and moved several tens of thousands of households back.
sentences.idiomatic: They pressed the victory, seized the enemy capital, gathered booty counted in the hundreds of millions, and resettled tens of thousands of households under their rule.

sentences.chinese: 成帝即位，加廆侍中，位特進。
sentences.literal: When Emperor Cheng took the throne, Kuang was added Palace Attendant-in-ordinary with specially advanced rank.
sentences.idiomatic: Upon Emperor Cheng's accession, Murong Hui received the title of palace attendant and the specially advanced precedence.

sentences.chinese: 咸和五年，又加開府儀同三司，固辭不受。
sentences.literal: In the fifth year of Xianhe, he was again given opening of office equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; he firmly declined and did not accept.
sentences.idiomatic: In Xianhe 5 he was again offered an independent establishment with parity to the three dukes, but he steadfastly refused the honor.

sentences.chinese: 廆嘗從容言曰：「獄者，人命之所懸也，不可以不慎。
sentences.literal: Kuang once said at ease: "Prisons are where human lives hang; one cannot but be careful.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Hui once remarked calmly, "The jail holds men's lives in the balance; nothing demands greater care.

sentences.chinese: 賢人君子，國家之基也，不可以不敬。
sentences.literal: Worthy men and gentlemen are the foundation of the state; one cannot but honor them.
sentences.idiomatic: Men of virtue are the bedrock of the realm; they must be treated with respect.

sentences.chinese: 稼穡者，國之本也，不可以不急。
sentences.literal: Grain farming is the root of the state; one cannot but treat it as urgent.
sentences.idiomatic: Agriculture is the state's root; it must be pressed without delay.

sentences.chinese: 酒色便佞，亂德之甚也，不可以不戒。
sentences.literal: Wine, sex, and smooth flattery are the utmost in disordering virtue; one cannot but guard against them.
sentences.idiomatic: Wine, lust, and sycophancy are the worst spoilers of moral conduct; they call for unsparing vigilance.

sentences.chinese: 」乃著《家令》數千言以申其旨。
sentences.literal: He then composed the "House Instructions" in several thousand words to set forth that meaning.
sentences.idiomatic: He therefore drafted the Family Instructions at length to spell out these maxims.

sentences.chinese: 遣使與太尉陶侃箋曰：
sentences.literal: He sent an envoy with a letter to Grand Commandant Tao Kan, saying:
sentences.idiomatic: He dispatched a messenger bearing a letter to Grand Commandant Tao Kan, which read:

sentences.chinese: 明公使君轂下：振德曜威，撫甯方夏，勞心文武，士馬無恙，欽高仰止，注情彌久。
sentences.literal: Illustrious lord beneath your carriage hubs: you raise virtue and display might, pacify and quiet the regions and the Hua; you weary heart and mind over civil and military affairs; troops and horses are without illness; I admire your height and gaze upward, and my regard has long been fixed.
sentences.idiomatic: To you, my lord, whose wheels we attend: you spread moral sway and show your power, bringing peace across the heartland; you exhaust yourself for civil and military matters, yet your men and mounts remain sound. Long have I looked up to your eminence with ever-deepening respect.

sentences.chinese: 王途險遠，隔以燕越，每瞻江湄，延首遐外。
sentences.literal: The royal road is perilous and far, cut off by Yan and Yue; whenever I gaze at the river's edge, I stretch my neck toward the distant beyond.
sentences.idiomatic: The path to the throne is long and dangerous, with Yan and Yue standing between us; each time I scan the riverbank my thoughts fly to what lies far away.

sentences.chinese: 天降艱難，禍害屢臻，舊都不守，奄為虜庭，使皇輿遷幸，假勢吳、楚。
sentences.literal: Heaven sent hardship; disasters came repeatedly; the old capital was not held and in a breath became a barbarian court, making the imperial palanquin remove in favor and borrow strength from Wu and Chu.
sentences.idiomatic: Heaven has sent affliction; calamities struck again and again. The former capital could not be held and overnight became barbarian ground, forcing the Son of Heaven to withdraw and lean on the power of Wu and Chu.

sentences.chinese: 大晉啟基、祚流萬節，天命未改，玄象著明，是以義烈之士深懷憤踴。
sentences.literal: Great Jin opened its foundation; fortune flows through myriad nodes; Heaven's mandate is not yet changed; the dark images are clear—therefore men of righteous ardor harbor deep indignant fervor.
sentences.idiomatic: Great Jin laid its foundation and its fortune should run through countless reigns; the Mandate stands unaltered and the stars proclaim it plainly. Men of loyal fire therefore nurse deep outrage.

sentences.chinese: 猥以功薄，受國殊寵，上不能掃除群羯，下不能身赴國難，仍縱賊臣，屢逼京輦。
sentences.literal: Vile though my merit is thin, I received the state's extraordinary favor; above I could not sweep away the mass of Jie, below I could not take my person to the state's hardship; still I let rebel ministers repeatedly press the capital palanquin.
sentences.idiomatic: Humble though my deeds are slight, I have received uncommon grace from the throne; yet I could not above extirpate the Jie hosts nor below throw myself into the national crisis, and I allowed traitors again and again to threaten the capital.

sentences.chinese: 王敦唱禍于前，蘇峻肆毒於後，凶暴過於董卓，惡逆甚於傕、汜，普天率土，誰不同忿！
sentences.literal: Wang Dun raised calamity in front, Su Jun spread poison afterward; fierce cruelty exceeded Dong Zhuo; evil rebellion was worse than Jue and Si; who under all heaven and all within the borders did not share the same indignation!
sentences.idiomatic: Wang Dun began the disaster and Su Jun followed with poison; their savagery outdid Dong Zhuo and their treason surpassed Li Jue and Guo Si. Who in the realm did not burn with the same anger?

sentences.chinese: 深怪文武之士，過荷朝榮，不能滅中原之寇，刷天下之恥。
sentences.literal: I deeply marvel that gentlemen of civil and military affairs, excessively bearing court glory, cannot extinguish the bandits of the Central Plain and brush away the shame of all under Heaven.
sentences.idiomatic: I am baffled that our civil and military officers, laden though they are with court honors, cannot crush the invaders of the heartland or wipe away the empire's disgrace.

sentences.chinese: 君侯植根江陽，發曜荊、衡，杖葉公之權，有包胥之志，而令白公、伍員殆得極其暴，竊為丘明恥之。
sentences.literal: Lord, you planted root in Jiangyang, sent forth radiance in Jing and Heng, staff Duke Ye's authority, have Bao Xu's ambition, yet you let Bai Gong and Wu Yuan nearly reach utmost violence; I privately am ashamed for Qiu Ming.
sentences.idiomatic: You, my lord, took root along the Yangzi and your brilliance reaches Jing and Heng; you wield the power of Duke Ye and the purpose of Shen Baoxu, yet you have allowed men in the mold of the White Duke and Wu Yuan to run to extremes of violence—I would be ashamed before Zuo Qiu Ming.

sentences.chinese: 區區楚國子重之徒，猶恥君弱、群臣不及先大夫，厲己戒眾，以服陳、鄭；
sentences.literal: The petty class of Zizhong of the state of Chu still was ashamed that the ruler was weak and that ministers did not match the earlier grand officers; they sharpened themselves and warned the host, thereby making Chen and Zheng submit.
sentences.idiomatic: Even minor figures such as Zizhong of Chu were shamed when their lord seemed feeble and the court fell short of the great ministers of old; they hardened themselves, rallied the army, and brought Chen and Zheng to heel.

sentences.chinese: 越之種蠡尚能弼佐句踐，取威黃池；
sentences.literal: Zhong and Li of Yue were still able to assist Gou Jian and take prestige at Huangchi.
sentences.idiomatic: Even Wen Zhong and Fan Li of Yue could steady Gou Jian and win standing at the Pool of Huang.

sentences.chinese: 況今吳土英賢比肩，而不輔翼聖主，陵江北伐。
sentences.literal: How much more now, when the soil of Wu has heroes and worthies shoulder to shoulder, yet they do not assist and wing the sage lord or cross the river north to campaign.
sentences.idiomatic: How much more may one expect now that the south of the Yangzi teems with talent, yet none will uphold the sage Son of Heaven or strike north across the great river.

sentences.chinese: 以義聲之直，討逆暴之羯，檄命舊邦之士，招懷存本之人，豈不若因風振落，頓阪走輪哉！
sentences.literal: With the straightness of righteous reputation, punish the rebellious, cruel Jie; issue proclamations to gentlemen of the old lands; summon and cherish those who preserve their roots—how would it not be like shaking leaves by wind or a wheel racing down a slope!
sentences.idiomatic: Under the banner of justice you could chastise the lawless Jie, call the gentry of the old domains to arms, and win over those who still cling to their allegiance—would it not be like wind stripping the trees or a chariot flying downhill?

sentences.chinese: 且孫氏之初，以長沙之眾摧破董卓，志匡漢室。
sentences.literal: Moreover at the beginning of the Sun clan, with the host of Changsha they crushed and broke Dong Zhuo, aiming to restore the Han house.
sentences.idiomatic: When the house of Sun first rose, they shattered Dong Zhuo with the army of Changsha, set on restoring the Han.

sentences.chinese: 雖中遇寇害，雅志不遂，原其心誠，乃忽身命。
sentences.literal: Although in the middle they met bandit harm and the lofty aim was not achieved, tracing their hearts' sincerity, they then disregarded body and life.
sentences.idiomatic: Though violence cut them short and their high purpose went unfulfilled, the earnestness of their intent shows they thought nothing of their lives.

sentences.chinese: 及權據揚、越，外杖周、張，內馮顧、陸，距魏亦壁，克取襄陽。
sentences.literal: When Quan held Yang and Yue, outwardly he leaned on Zhou and Zhang, inwardly he relied on Gu and Lu; resisting Wei at the rampart of Yi, he overcame and took Xiangyang.
sentences.idiomatic: When Sun Quan held Yang and Yue, he used Zhou and Zhang abroad and Gu and Lu at home; he held Wei at bay along the Red Cliff line and took Xiangyang.

sentences.chinese: 自茲以降，世主相襲，咸能侵逼徐、豫，令魏朝旰食。
sentences.literal: From this downward, generation after generation of lords inherited one another; all were able to invade and press Xu and Yu, making the Wei court eat late.
sentences.idiomatic: Thereafter each ruler in turn could harry Xu and Yu and keep the Wei court from dining at ease.

sentences.chinese: 不知今之江表為賢俊匿智，藏其勇略邪？
sentences.literal: I do not know whether today's south of the river is worthies hiding wisdom and concealing their courage and strategy.
sentences.idiomatic: I cannot tell whether the Yangzi region now hides its able men and muffles their courage and design.

sentences.chinese: 將呂蒙、淩統高蹤曠世哉？
sentences.literal: Or is it that Lü Meng and Ling Tong left high tracks separated by ages?
sentences.idiomatic: Or have we simply lost sight of towering exemplars such as Lü Meng and Ling Tong?

sentences.chinese: 況今凶羯虐暴，中州人士逼迫勢促，其顛沛之危，甚於累卵。
sentences.literal: How much more now, when the fierce Jie are cruel and violent, men and affairs of the central provinces are pressed and the situation is urgent; their overturned peril is worse than stacked eggs.
sentences.idiomatic: Today the savage Jie ravage the land; the gentry of the Central Plain are trapped in an ever-tightening vise, and their plight is more fragile than a tower of eggs.

sentences.chinese: 假號之強，眾心所去，敵有釁矣，易可震盪。
sentences.literal: The strength of a borrowed title is what the hearts of the masses turn from; the enemy has a crack; it is easy to shake and overturn.
sentences.idiomatic: Their counterfeit majesty is hollow, popular feeling has deserted them, and the foe shows a fissure—they could be toppled with a shove.

sentences.chinese: 王郎、袁術雖自詐偽，皆基淺根微，禍不旋踵，此皆君侯之所聞見者矣。
sentences.literal: Although Wang Lang and Yuan Shu were themselves false and deceitful, all had shallow base and slight root; calamity did not turn on the heel—these are things my lord has heard and seen.
sentences.idiomatic: Wang Lang and Yuan Shu were impostors, yet their power rested on sand; ruin overtook them before they could turn—all of which you yourself have witnessed.

sentences.chinese: 王司徒清虛寡欲，善於全己，昔曹參亦綜此道，著畫一之稱也。
sentences.literal: Minister Wang is clear, empty, and few in desires, good at preserving himself; long ago Cao Can also practiced this way and bore the name of 'unified governance.'
sentences.idiomatic: Director Wang Dao is spare in appetite and adept at keeping himself whole; Cao Can of old trod the same path and won praise for ruling with a single, steady stroke.

sentences.chinese: 庾公居元舅之尊，處申伯之任，超然高蹈，明智之權。
sentences.literal: Lord Yu occupies the honor of chief maternal uncle, holds the duty of Shen Bo, transcends and treads high, with the balance of clear wisdom.
sentences.idiomatic: Yu Liang stands as the emperor's uncle in the mold of the Earl of Shen—aloof, principled, and judicious in the scales of power.

sentences.chinese: 廆於寇難之際，受大晉累世之恩，自恨絕域，無益聖朝，徒系心萬里，望風懷憤。
sentences.literal: Kuang, amid the time of bandit hardship, received favor through generations from Great Jin; he himself hated being cut off beyond the frontier, without benefit to the sage court, only tying heart ten thousand li, gazing at the wind and cherishing indignation.
sentences.idiomatic: In these years of invasion I have enjoyed the Jin throne's favor for generations; I chafe at my remoteness and my inability to aid the court, and can only fix my thoughts a thousand leagues away, nursing righteous anger.

sentences.chinese: 今海內之望，足為楚、漢輕重者，惟在君侯。
sentences.literal: Now the hopes of all within the seas, sufficient to be the weight between Chu and Han, rest solely with my lord.
sentences.idiomatic: Today the expectations that can tip the balance, as between Chu and Han, rest on you alone, my lord.

sentences.chinese: 若戮力盡心，悉五州之眾，據兗、豫之郊，使向義之士倒戈釋甲，則羯寇必滅，國恥必除。
sentences.literal: If you join strength and exhaust heart, gather the hosts of five provinces, occupy the outskirts of Yan and Yu, and make men who turn to righteousness cast aside arms and armor, then the Jie bandits will certainly be destroyed and the shame of the state certainly removed.
sentences.idiomatic: If you muster the five provinces, hold the approaches to Yan and Yu, and turn loyal men to lay down their arms in your cause, the Jie foe will fall and the dynasty's humiliation can be wiped away.

sentences.chinese: 廆在一方，敢不竭命。
sentences.literal: Kuang, in one quarter, how dare he not exhaust his mandate.
sentences.idiomatic: On my distant frontier I shall spare no effort in your service.

sentences.chinese: 孤軍輕進，不足使勒畏首畏尾，則懷舊之士欲為內應，無由自發故也。
sentences.literal: A lone army lightly advancing is insufficient to make Le fear head and fear tail, which is why men who cherish the old wish to be inner responders yet have no way to rise on their own.
sentences.idiomatic: A single column pushing forward lightly will not make Shi Le look to front and rear; that is why loyalists in the north who would rise within cannot strike without a coordinated blow.

sentences.chinese: 故遠陳寫，言不宣盡。
sentences.literal: Therefore from afar I state it in writing; words cannot declare all.
sentences.idiomatic: I therefore set down these lines from afar, knowing they cannot say everything I feel.

sentences.chinese: 廆使者遭風沒海。
sentences.literal: Kuang's envoy met wind and sank in the sea.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Hui's messenger was lost at sea in a gale.

sentences.chinese: 其後廆更寫前箋，並齎其東夷校尉封抽、行遼東相韓矯等三十餘人疏上侃府曰：
sentences.literal: Afterward Kuang again wrote the earlier letter and together sent his Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, acting Liaodong Chancellor Han Jiao, and more than thirty others with a memorial up to Kan's office, saying:
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Hui then redrafted his earlier letter and, together with Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, acting Liaodong administrator Han Jiao, and more than thirty others, submitted a joint memorial to Tao Kan's headquarters:

sentences.chinese: 自古有國有家，鮮不極盛而衰。
sentences.literal: From antiquity, for those who had states and houses, rarely have they not, at utmost flourish, declined.
sentences.idiomatic: Since ancient times few realms have not, after reaching their height, begun to wane.

sentences.chinese: 自大晉龍興，克平㟭、會，神武之略，邁蹤前史。
sentences.literal: From Great Jin's dragon rise, it overcame and pacified Min and Kuai; the strategy of spirit-like martial prowess tracks the former histories.
sentences.idiomatic: When Great Jin rose like a dragon it subdued Min and Kuai; its military genius stands with the annals of old.

sentences.chinese: 惠皇之末，後黨構難，禍結京畿，釁成公族，遂使羯寇乘虛，傾覆諸夏，舊都淪滅，山陵毀掘，人神悲悼，幽明發憤。
sentences.literal: At the end of Emperor Hui, the later faction contrived hardship; disaster knotted in the capital region; rift formed among the ducal clans; thereupon they let the Jie bandits exploit the void, overturn all Xia, the old capital sink and perish, hills and tombs destroyed and dug; man and spirit mourned; dark and bright sent forth indignation.
sentences.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui's late reign the empress's faction sowed strife; calamity gripped the capital and blood feuds split the imperial kin. The Jie then poured through the breach, overturned the heartland, took the old capital, and violated the imperial tombs, drawing grief from men and gods alike.

sentences.chinese: 昔獫狁之強，匈奴之盛，未有如今日羯寇之暴，跨躡華裔，盜稱尊號者也。
sentences.literal: Long ago the strength of the Xianyun, the flourishing of the Xiongnu, did not reach today's Jie bandits' violence, striding Hu and Yi, stealing and calling a honored title.
sentences.idiomatic: Neither the Xianyun at their strongest nor the Xiongnu at their height matched the brutality of today's Jie, who stride across Huaxia and the borderlands and usurp the imperial style.

sentences.chinese: 天祚有晉，挺授英傑。
sentences.literal: Heaven's blessing has Jin; it raises and grants heroic outstanding men.
sentences.idiomatic: Heaven favors Jin and has furnished it with heroes.

sentences.chinese: 車騎將軍慕容廆自弱冠蒞國，忠於王室，明允恭肅，志在立勳。
sentences.literal: Chariots-and-cavalry General Murong Kuang, from weak cap ascending the state, was loyal to the royal house, clear, trustworthy, respectful, and solemn; his aim lay in establishing merit.
sentences.idiomatic: General of Chariots and Cavalry Murong Hui took the realm in his youth, served the dynasty with loyalty, and showed judgment, good faith, and grave decorum, intent on winning honor for the throne.

sentences.chinese: 屬海內分崩，皇輿遷幸，元皇中興，初唱大業，肅祖繼統，蕩平江外。
sentences.literal: When all within the seas split apart and the imperial palanquin removed in favor, the Yuan Emperor restored the line and first raised the great enterprise; the Su Ancestor continued the line and swept the region beyond the river.
sentences.idiomatic: As the realm shattered and the court withdrew south, Emperor Yuan revived the house and began the great restoration; Emperor Ming carried the work forward and cleared the lands beyond the Yangzi.

sentences.chinese: 廆雖限以山海，隔以羯寇，翹首引領，系心京師，常假寤寐，欲憂國忘身。
sentences.literal: Although Kuang was bounded by mountains and seas and cut off by Jie bandits, he craned head and stretched neck, tied heart to the capital, often feigned waking and sleeping, wishing to worry for the state and forget himself.
sentences.idiomatic: Though mountains and seas hemmed him in and the Jie stood between him and the throne, Murong Hui strained toward the capital, waking and sleeping with the court on his mind, ready to sacrifice himself for the realm.

sentences.chinese: 貢篚相尋，連舟載路，戎不稅駕，動成義舉。
sentences.literal: Tribute baskets followed one another; boats linked loaded the road; weapons did not unhitch teams; movement became righteous rising.
sentences.idiomatic: Tribute trains followed one another, barges crowded the waterways, and his hosts never stood down—each move served the loyal cause.

sentences.chinese: 今羯寇滔天，怙其丑類，樹基趙、魏，跨略燕、齊。
sentences.literal: Now the Jie bandits flood heaven; they rely on their ugly kind, plant foundation in Zhao and Wei, stride and seize Yan and Qi.
sentences.idiomatic: The Jie marauders now swell like a flood; they lean on their own kind, root themselves in Zhao and Wei, and span Yan and Qi.

sentences.chinese: 廆雖率義眾，誅討大逆，然管仲相齊，猶曰寵不足以禦下，況廆輔翼王室，有匡霸之功，而位卑爵輕，九命未加，非所以寵異籓翰，敦獎殊勳者也。
sentences.literal: Although Kuang leads righteous hosts and punishes and attacks great rebellion, yet Guan Zhong assisting Qi still said favor was insufficient to control subordinates; how much more Kuang assisting and winging the royal house, having merit in restoring hegemony, yet position is low and noble rank is light, the nine bestowals not yet added—this is not the means to favor and distinguish a frontier screen or earnestly encourage extraordinary merit.
sentences.idiomatic: Though Murong Hui leads loyal armies against the arch-rebel, even Guan Zhong, minister to Qi, warned that indulgence alone cannot command subordinates—how much less can Hui, who props the throne and has the work of a hegemon behind him, be left in low office and light rank without the highest honors? Such treatment neither marks a bulwark marquis nor rewards uncommon service.

sentences.chinese: 方今詔命隔絕，王路險遠，貢使往來，動彌年載。
sentences.literal: At present edicts and commands are cut off; the royal road is perilous and far; tribute envoys come and go, moving often a full year.
sentences.idiomatic: Imperial orders no longer reach us easily; the road to the throne is long and dangerous; envoys shuttling tribute may be a year on the way.

sentences.chinese: 今燕之舊壤，北周沙漠，東盡樂浪，西暨代山，南極冀方，而悉為虜庭，非復國家之域。
sentences.literal: Now Yan's old soil, north girds the desert, east ends at Lelang, west reaches Mount Dai, south reaches Jizhou, yet all is barbarian court, no longer the state's domain.
sentences.idiomatic: The ancient land of Yan—ringed on the north by the desert, reaching Lelang in the east, Mount Dai in the west, and Jizhou in the south—has become barbarian ground and is lost to the dynasty.

sentences.chinese: 將佐等以為宜遠遵周室，近准漢初，進封廆為燕王，行大將軍事，上以總統諸部，下以割損賊境。
sentences.literal: Generals and assistants judged it fitting, far following the Zhou house, near patterning early Han, to advance and enfeoff Kuang as King of Yan, acting grand general's affairs, above thereby to overall command the various divisions, below thereby to cut and harm the bandit territory.
sentences.idiomatic: His officers held that, following the Zhou model in spirit and the early Han in practice, Murong Hui should be advanced as king of Yan with acting powers of grand general—uniting the tribes above and biting into enemy ground below.

sentences.chinese: 使冀州之人望風向化。
sentences.literal: Make the people of Jizhou gaze at the wind and turn to transformation.
sentences.idiomatic: Let the folk of Jizhou feel the moral breeze and come over to the rightful cause.

sentences.chinese: 廆得祗承詔命，率合諸國，奉辭夷逆，以成桓文之功，苟利社稷，專之可也。
sentences.literal: If Kuang can respectfully receive edict and mandate, lead and join the various states, offer rhetoric against the barbarian rebels, thereby completing the merit of Huan and Wen, if it profits the altars of soil and grain, specializing it is permissible.
sentences.idiomatic: If Murong Hui may take up the imperial charge, rally the states, and move against the barbarian usurpers in the manner of Duke Huan and Duke Wen, he may act on his own authority whenever the altars of state stand to gain.

sentences.chinese: 而廆固執謙光，守節彌高，每詔所加，讓動積年，非將佐等所能敦逼。
sentences.literal: Yet Kuang firmly holds modest light; guarding integrity grows higher; whenever an edict adds honor, he declines in movement accumulated years—not something generals and assistants can earnestly press.
sentences.idiomatic: Yet Murong Hui clings to modesty; the longer he holds his integrity, the loftier it seems, and each new honor draws refusals that drag on for years—no pressure from his staff can move him.

sentences.chinese: 今區區所陳，不欲苟相崇重，而愚情至心，實為國計。
sentences.literal: Now the petty that we state, we do not wish lightly to mutually exalt and honor, yet foolish feeling and utmost heart truly are for the state's plan.
sentences.idiomatic: We do not offer this out of mere flattery; our plain loyalty is truly bent on the realm's interest.

sentences.chinese: 侃報抽等書，其略曰：「車騎將軍憂國忘身，貢篚載路，羯賊求和，執使送之，西討段國，北伐塞外，遠綏索頭，荒服以獻。
sentences.literal: Kan replied in writing to Chou and the others; the gist said: 'Chariots-and-cavalry General worries for the state and forgets himself; tribute baskets load the road; Jie bandits sought peace; he seized envoys and sent them; west he campaigned against the Duan state, north he campaigned beyond the passes, far he soothed the Suotou, wild submission came to offer.'
sentences.idiomatic: Tao Kan wrote back to Feng Chou and his colleagues, in substance: 'The general of chariots and cavalry thinks only of the state; tribute fills the roads. When the Jie sued for peace he seized their envoys and forwarded them; he struck the Duan domain in the west, campaigned beyond the frontier in the north, pacified the Suotou in the distance, and brought wild tribes to submit.'

sentences.chinese: 惟北部未賓，屢遣征伐。
sentences.literal: Only the north quarter has not submitted; repeatedly he sends campaigns and attacks.
sentences.idiomatic: Only the northern tribes still hold out; he has repeatedly sent forces against them.

sentences.chinese: 又知東方官號，高下齊班，進無統攝之權，退無等差之降，欲進車騎為燕王，一二具之。
sentences.literal: Also knowing eastern offices' titles, high and low equal in ranks, advancing there is no overall command authority, retreating there is no gradation of demotion, wishing to advance chariot-cavalry as King of Yan, one by one set them forth.
sentences.idiomatic: I also hear that eastern offices are ranked without clear hierarchy—neither unified command above nor graded demotion below—and you wish to raise the general of chariots and cavalry to king of Yan; lay out each point in order.

sentences.chinese: 夫功成進爵，古之成制也。
sentences.literal: Merit accomplished and advancing noble rank is antiquity's completed regulation.
sentences.idiomatic: Promoting rank after deeds are done is an ancient and settled rule.

sentences.chinese: 車騎雖未能為官摧勒，然忠義竭誠。
sentences.literal: Chariot-cavalry although not yet able for the court to crush Le, yet loyalty and righteousness exhaust sincerity.
sentences.idiomatic: Though the general has not yet broken Shi Le for the court, his good faith is beyond question.

sentences.chinese: 今騰箋上聽，可不遲速，當任天臺也。
sentences.literal: Now I soar a memorial upward for hearing; it cannot be slow or fast; it ought to await the Celestial Terrace.
sentences.idiomatic: I shall forward your memorial to the throne; timing is not for me to decide—the central government must rule on it.

sentences.chinese: 」朝議未定。
sentences.literal: The court deliberation was not settled.
sentences.idiomatic: Court opinion remained divided.

sentences.chinese: 八年，廆卒，乃止。
sentences.literal: In the eighth year, Kuang died; thereupon it stopped.
sentences.idiomatic: In the eighth year Murong Hui died, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.chinese: 時年六十五，在位四十九年。
sentences.literal: At the time his years were sixty-five; on the throne forty-nine years.
sentences.idiomatic: He was sixty-five and had held power forty-nine years.

sentences.chinese: 帝遣使者策贈大將軍、開府儀同三司，諡曰襄。
sentences.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys with patent bestowing grand general, opening office equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; posthumous name Xiang.
sentences.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys with a patent naming him grand general with an independent establishment equal to the three dukes and the posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.chinese: 及俊僭號，偽諡武宣皇帝。
sentences.literal: When Jun usurped title, false posthumous Emperor Wu Xuan.
sentences.idiomatic: When Murong Jun seized the imperial style he gave him the spurious posthumous name Emperor Wu Xuan.

sentences.chinese: 裴嶷，字文冀，河東聞喜人也。
sentences.literal: Pei Yi, style Wenji, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
sentences.idiomatic: Pei Yi, courtesy name Wenji, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.chinese: 父昶，司隸校尉。
sentences.literal: His father Chang, Metropolitan Superintendent.
sentences.idiomatic: His father Pei Chang had served as metropolitan commandant.

sentences.chinese: 嶷清方有幹略，累遷至中書侍郎，轉給事黃門郎、滎陽太守。
sentences.literal: Yi was clear and upright with capacity and strategy, repeatedly promoted to Palace Secretariat Vice Director, transferred to palace attendant yellow-gate gentleman, Xingyang Administrator.
sentences.idiomatic: Pei Yi was principled and able; he rose to vice director of the palace secretariat, then became a palace attendant and gentleman at the yellow gate, and finally prefect of Xingyang.

sentences.chinese: 屬天下亂，嶷兄武先為玄菟太守，嶷遂求為昌黎太守。
sentences.literal: It fell under all under Heaven in disorder; Yi's elder brother Wu first was Xuandu Administrator; Yi thereupon sought to be Changli Administrator.
sentences.idiomatic: When the realm fell into chaos, his elder brother Pei Wu was already prefect of Xuandu; Pei Yi therefore asked for the post at Changli.

sentences.chinese: 至郡，久之，武卒，嶷被征，乃將武子開送喪俱南。
sentences.literal: When he reached the commandery, after a long time Wu died; Yi was summoned; then he led Wu's son Kai sending the funeral, together south.
sentences.idiomatic: He had been in office some time when Pei Wu died; summoned to court, he escorted his brother's son Pei Kai south to bury him.

sentences.chinese: 既達遼西，道路梗塞，乃與開投廆。
sentences.literal: Having reached Liaoxi, roads were blocked and obstructed; then together with Kai he threw himself to Kuang.
sentences.idiomatic: When they reached Liaoxi the roads were impassable, so he and Pei Kai took refuge with Murong Hui.

sentences.chinese: 時諸流寓之士見廆草創，並懷去就。
sentences.literal: At the time various drifting gentlemen saw Kuang grass founding, all cherished staying or going.
sentences.idiomatic: The refugees who saw Murong Hui founding his state hesitated whether to stay or leave.

sentences.chinese: 嶷首定名分，為群士啟行。
sentences.literal: Yi first fixed names and ranks, for the host of gentlemen opening the march.
sentences.idiomatic: Pei Yi was first to settle ranks and duties and set the example that rallied the scholars.

sentences.chinese: 廆甚悅，以嶷為長史，委以軍國之謀。
sentences.literal: Kuang was very pleased; he appointed Yi Chief Clerk and entrusted him with army and state's planning.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Hui was delighted, named him chief clerk, and gave him charge of civil and military planning.

sentences.chinese: 及悉獨官寇逼城下，外內騷動，廆問策於嶷，嶷曰：「悉獨官雖擁大眾，軍無號令，眾無部陣，若簡精兵，乘其無備，則成擒耳。
sentences.literal: When Xiduguan bandits pressed beneath the walls, outer and inner were in turmoil; Kuang asked strategy of Yi; Yi said: 'Although Xiduguan holds a great host, the army has no commands, the host has no battle lines; if you pick crack troops and ride his unpreparedness, then he is taken alive.'
sentences.idiomatic: When Xiduguan drove up to the walls and panic spread inside and out, Murong Hui asked Pei Yi for a plan. Pei Yi replied, 'Xiduguan's horde is huge but undisciplined and without formation; elite troops catching him off guard will bring him in chains.'

sentences.chinese: 」廆從之，遂陷寇營。
sentences.literal: Kuang followed it; thereupon he fell on the bandit camp.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Hui took the advice and stormed the enemy camp.

sentences.chinese: 廆威德於此甚振，將遣使獻捷於建鄴，妙簡行人，令嶷將命。
sentences.literal: Kuang's might and virtue here greatly shook; he wished to send envoys to present victory at Jianye, subtly picking travelers, ordering Yi to bear the command.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Hui's prestige soared; he meant to report his victory to Jianye and, choosing his envoy with care, sent Pei Yi on the mission.

sentences.chinese: 初，朝廷以廆僻在荒遠，猶以邊裔之豪處之。
sentences.literal: At first the court, because Kuang was tucked in wild distance, still treated him as a frontier chieftain.
sentences.idiomatic: At first the court, seeing Murong Hui far off in the wilderness, still handled him as a border magnate.

sentences.chinese: 嶷既使至，盛言廆威略，又知四海英賢並為其用，舉朝改觀焉。
sentences.literal: When Yi had arrived as envoy, he greatly declared Kuang's might and strategy, and also knew that heroes and worthies of the four seas all were used by him; the whole court changed its view.
sentences.idiomatic: Once Pei Yi reached the capital he expounded Murong Hui's power and design and showed how men of talent from every quarter flocked to his banner; the whole court revised its opinion.

sentences.chinese: 嶷將還，帝試留嶷以觀之，嶷辭曰：「臣世荷朝恩，濯纓華省，因事遠寄，投跡荒遐。
sentences.literal: When Yi was about to return, the emperor tried detaining Yi to observe him; Yi declined, saying: 'Your subject's house for generations bore court favor, washed tassel in splendid ministry, because of affairs lodged far, cast tracks in wild distance.'
sentences.idiomatic: As Pei Yi prepared to leave, the emperor tested him by offering a post at court. Pei Yi refused: 'My family has long enjoyed imperial grace; I served in the high ministries, then was driven far afield and took refuge in the frontier.'

sentences.chinese: 今遭開泰，得睹朝廷，復賜恩詔，即留京輦，於臣之私，誠為厚幸。
sentences.literal: Now encountering open peace, able to see the court, again granted favor edict, then staying in the capital region—for your subject's private feeling, truly it is thick fortune.
sentences.idiomatic: Now, in this calmer age, I have seen the throne again and received a gracious summons to remain—personally that would be a great blessing.

sentences.chinese: 顧以皇居播遷，山陵幽辱，慕容龍驤將軍越在遐表，乃心王室，慷慨之誠，義感天地，方掃平中壤，奉迎皇輿，故遣使臣，萬里表誠。
sentences.literal: But because the imperial residence is cast about, hills and tombs are in dark insult, Murong Dragon-Soaring General is beyond the distant border, his heart toward the royal house, generous and righteous sincerity, righteousness moves heaven and earth, about to sweep level the central soil, respectfully welcome the imperial palanquin, therefore sending envoy ministers, ten thousand li declaring sincerity.
sentences.idiomatic: Yet the court is in exile and the tombs lie shamed; General Murong Hui, though far away, keeps the dynasty in his heart with a passion that moves heaven and earth. He means to clear the heartland and escort the imperial train home, and he sent me across ten thousand li to prove his loyalty.

sentences.chinese: 今若留臣，必謂國家遺其僻陋，孤其丹心，使懷義懈怠。
sentences.literal: Now if you detain your subject, they will certainly say the state casts off his remote rusticness, isolates his cinnabar heart, making those who cherish righteousness slacken.
sentences.idiomatic: If you keep me here, men will say the court scorns his distant realm and chills his loyal heart, sapping the zeal of those who would serve the throne.

sentences.chinese: 是以微臣區區忘身為國，貪還反命耳。
sentences.literal: Therefore this petty subject, petty and small, forgets body for the state, greedy to return and report mandate.
sentences.idiomatic: That is why I set my own safety aside for the realm and am eager only to return with my answer.

sentences.chinese: 」帝曰：「卿言是也。
sentences.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are right.
sentences.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You speak rightly.

sentences.chinese: 」乃遣嶷還。
sentences.literal: Thereupon he sent Yi back.
sentences.idiomatic: He therefore let Pei Yi depart.

sentences.chinese: 廆後謂群僚曰：「裴長史名重中朝，而降屈於此，豈非天以授孤也。
sentences.literal: Kuang afterward said to the host of officials: 'Chief Clerk Pei's name weighed in the central court, yet bent low here—is it not Heaven that gave him to me?'
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Hui later told his officers, 'Chief Clerk Pei was famed at court yet stooped to serve me—can this be anything but Heaven's gift?'

sentences.chinese: 」出為遼東相，轉樂浪太守。
sentences.literal: He went out as Liaodong Chancellor, transferred to Lelang Administrator.
sentences.idiomatic: Pei Yi was sent out as administrator of Liaodong, then moved to prefect of Lelang.

sentences.chinese: 高瞻，字子前，渤海蓚人也。
sentences.literal: Gao Zhan, style Ziqian, was a man of Tiao in Bohai.
sentences.idiomatic: Gao Zhan, courtesy name Ziqian, was a native of Tiao in Bohai.

sentences.chinese: 少而英爽有俊才，身長八尺二寸。
sentences.literal: In youth he was heroic and bright with outstanding talent; his body was eight chi two cun in height.
sentences.idiomatic: In his youth he was dashing and gifted and stood eight chi two cun tall.

sentences.chinese: 光熙中，調補尚書郎。
sentences.literal: In the Guangxi era, he was transferred and supplemented Secretariat Gentleman.
sentences.idiomatic: During the Guangxi reign he was appointed gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.chinese: 屬永嘉之亂，還鄉里，乃與父老議曰：「今皇綱不振，兵革雲擾，此郡沃壤，憑固河海，若兵荒歲儉，必為寇庭，非謂圖安之所。
sentences.literal: It fell under the Yongjia turmoil; he returned to his village; then together with village elders he deliberated, saying: 'Now the imperial net does not shake; weapons and armor rise like clouds; this commandery is fertile soil, relying firm on river and sea; if weapons famine years are lean, it will certainly become a bandit court—not what is called a place to seek peace.'
sentences.idiomatic: When the Yongjia upheaval came he went home and said to the elders, 'The dynasty's grip is failing and war spreads like clouds. Our county is rich land defended by river and sea; in famine and turmoil it will become raiders' ground—not a haven for quiet life.'

sentences.chinese: 王彭祖先在幽、薊，據燕、代之資，兵強國富，可以托也。
sentences.literal: Wang Pengzu long ago was in You and Ji, occupying Yan and Dai's resources, troops strong state rich, can be entrusted.
sentences.idiomatic: Wang Jun has long held You and Ji, commands the wealth of Yan and Dai, and fields a strong, prosperous host—we can lean on him.

sentences.chinese: 諸君以為何如？
sentences.literal: What do the gentlemen think?
sentences.idiomatic: What say you all?
